## TL;DR

I walked the Inbox and Review board columns, and the phone work queue that replaces them below the mobile breakpoint, at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The layout held: long unbroken titles stay inside the column, the column header shows a visible keyboard focus ring at every width, and the phone queue's loading, error and empty states fit the viewport. One real defect showed up: an empty Inbox or Review column said only "—". I changed the five status columns to say what is missing in plain English, and I did the same for the status-filter view, which had the same bare dash. The scoped check is the gate for this handoff.

## Work and rationale

Inbox and Review are not routes. They are status columns defined in `src/ui-app/src/stores/repo.ts` and rendered by `BoardColumn.vue` on the Work page. On phones the Work page shows `MobileWorkQueue.vue` instead. So I audited those two components, not a route.

Following the repo's existing QA pattern (`work-board-moves-qa-browser.test.ts`), I wrote `src/ui-app/tests/inbox-review-pages-qa-browser.test.ts`. It mounts the real components in jsdom, serializes the DOM, and renders it in headless WebKit at the three widths with the built global stylesheet. Each width checks four things: no element sits outside the viewport and the document does not widen; empty copy is words, not a dash; the column header shows a focus ring on Tab; and the phone queue's loading, error and empty states fit.

The walk found one defect. `BoardColumn` defaulted `emptyText` to "—", and `WorkView` only overrides it for draft. So an empty Inbox or Review column rendered a bare dash in the default theme. The gen-z theme already had per-column copy, which made the plain theme the odd one out. The fix is a `PLAIN_EMPTY` map keyed by column id, used when the caller passes no text. I covered all five status columns, not just Inbox and Review, because they share the same fallback path. The default prop changed from "—" to "", so the fallback runs whenever no text is passed.

The status-filter column (`/work?status=…`) passed `empty-text="—"` explicitly, so filtering to Inbox would still show a dash. I changed it to pass the dash only for draft. The existing draft assertions in `board-column-labels.test.ts` lock that behavior, so I left draft's dash alone.

I did not run the full Work page. It needs the API and the auth shell, and I cannot run `repoos serve` from a managed session. The component-level audit covers the surfaces that actually differ at these widths. Full-page behavior at the widths is the open part; a human preview would cover it.

## Approaches tried

My first run of the new test used the repo-root vitest, which failed to compile the `.vue` files. The UI config is `src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`, so I ran it with `--config`. The focus check presses Tab in WebKit and reads the computed outline or box-shadow of the focused header. That measures what a user sees rather than what a stylesheet rule says.

For the empty copy, the draft test reads `props("emptyText")`, so draft's explicit dash has to stay in the caller. The fallback map covers the other columns.

## Challenges and blockers

The draft test asserts an explicit dash for the filtered draft view. My first change removed the attribute from the filter column, which made that prop `""` and would have broken the assertion. The conditional `draft ? "—" : undefined` keeps the prop value and still shows the copy for every other status.

The phone queue and column-level checks passed on the first real run, so the overflow assertions were not tested against a failure. I checked the long-title case by construction (a 150+ character unbroken identifier), not against a real layout bug.

## Key learnings

The copy defect was the kind a visual pass tends to wave through: a dash is not broken, just unhelpful. Asserting that the empty text is not a bare dash made it a failing test first. A column without a map entry still falls back to the dash, which is the intended behavior for draft.
